source: AgentRx — Microsoft Research failure taxonomy for agent trajectories
summary: Domain-agnostic framework that localizes the critical failure step in a failed agent trajectory using a grounded 9-category taxonomy (Plan Adherence Failure, Hallucination, Invalid Invocation, etc.). Includes a benchmark of 115 annotated failed runs across τ-bench, Flash, and Magentic-One.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps directly to HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification). The taxonomy and failure-localization logic could inform how AgentForge classifies subprocess failures before deciding to retry vs. escalate.

source: E-mem arXiv:2601.21714 — multi-agent episodic context reconstruction
summary: A multi-agent approach to episodic context reconstruction for LLM agent memory, enabling agents to reconstruct relevant past context across long horizons.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps to HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory injection into planner and executor prompts). Confirms the importance of episodic retrieval for long-running orchestrators.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel merge, GA April 2026)
summary: Microsoft merged AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into a single MIT-licensed Agent Framework 1.0 (GA April 3 2026), adding multi-agent orchestration, MCP interoperability, episodic procedural memory, graph-based workflow engine, and A2A support for .NET and Python.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — different language ecosystem (.NET/Python SDK); AgentForge is a Node.js/TypeScript Fastify backend with CLI subprocess agents. The episodic memory module maps to HID-188 but no actionable gap beyond existing open issue.

summary: LangGraph 1.2.16 and LangChain 1.4.6 (as of Oct 17 2026) added per-call human approval, node timeouts and error handlers, built-in MCP support, and DeltaChannel for cheaper long context threads. Weekly release cadence, several features still beta.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Python-only ecosystem; AgentForge runs Node.js TypeScript. Human approval and node timeouts conceptually overlap with AgentForge's policy engine but are already implemented differently. No actionable gap beyond existing architecture.

source: Google SpecOps '26 — Spec-Driven Test Generation (contract-first approach)
summary: Proposes having an agent document pre-conditions, post-conditions, and undefined behaviors (contracts) before writing tests. Shows direct prompting misses edge cases; spec-first reasoning improves test coverage significantly.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps directly to HID-135 (synthesize acceptance-test harness from approved plan before implementation). The contract-first framing reinforces deriving tests from the approved plan's acceptance criteria.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework — Episodic Procedural Memory (public preview 2026)
summary: Microsoft Agent Framework ships episodic procedural memory in public preview: records action sequences, tool selections, and intermediate decisions as episodes, then retrieves the closest match for similar new requests.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — overlaps with HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory). Confirms industry direction; no new gap beyond what HID-188 already scopes.

source: Karpathy multi-agent nanochat experiment (8 agents as research org, 2026)
summary: Karpathy ran 8 agents (4 Claude, 4 Codex) each on a GPU, acting as a small research organization doing pretraining experiments on his nanochat codebase. The experiment reportedly failed. He coins 'agentic engineering' as the successor to vibe coding.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — describes a research-lab experiment, not an orchestration framework pattern. AgentForge already handles multi-stage sequential orchestration; parallel GPU-per-agent setups are out of scope (rejected as premature per architecture notes).

source: triage Python library (PyCon JP 2026 — 9-type agent failure classifier)
summary: Community Python library that classifies agent failures by inspecting the recorded trajectory, returning one of 9 typed causes (WRONG_TOOL_CALLED, LOOP_DETECTED, etc.) and routing each to a recovery action. Self-reported 52% recall / 100% precision.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — maps conceptually to HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification). Python-only and early-stage (self-reported metrics); no actionable gap beyond HID-167.
